references.text: Repeats the same phrase that there was no king in Israel, emphasizing the theme of lawlessness and chaos during this period.
Uses the same formulation that there was no king in Israel, introducing yet another account of moral decay.
Concludes the book of Judges with exactly the same statement, summarizing the entire book's theme that everyone did what was right in their own eyes.
Moses warns against doing what is right in one's own eyes, a practice whose consequences are shown in the book of Judges.
Proverbs warns against following one's own way, which seems right in one's own eyes, in contrast to listening to advice.
Describes how people regard their own ways as right, while the Lord tests the heart.
Isaiah pronounces woe on those who are wise in their own eyes, the same attitude described in Judges.
